displayText: Now the slide. E to the x plus one is the same curve moved one unit left. Sliding doesn't tilt anything. Each tangent just slides along with its point, keeping its slope. So the gradient still equals the height, and the derivative of e to the x plus one is just e to the x plus one. Back to your guess. At x equals zero, the slid curve is about two point seven high, so its slope is about two point seven. The squashed curve is only one high there, with a slope of two. So the slid curve is steeper at zero only because it's higher. What matters is how the gradient compares with the height.
